newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says applies for telecom licence in U.S..
newsitem.headline: NTT says applies for telecom licence in U.S..

text.p: Japanese telecoms giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) said on Friday its wholly owned U.S. unit had applied for a licence to run telecommunications services between the United States and other countries besides Japan.
The U.S. unit -- NTT America Inc -- on Thursday filed for approval from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to start offering telecommunications services, NTT said.
The federal agency will publish the contents of the application and accept any objections from competitors in the next 21 days before making a decision.
NTT said in a statement that if the application is approved it plans to start with the resale of lines within the United States as well as those between the United States and Britain.
NTT said it hopes the FCC will make a swift decision.
NTT, which last month won regulatory approval to offer international services as part of its restructuring, has acquired telecom licences in Britain, Germany and France.

But analysts remained sceptical about any quick approval from U.S. authorities, citing the fact that it took more than a year for Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD) to obtain a similar U.S. licence because of its dominant position in Japan's international telephone market.

NTT, boasting strong ties with Japanese multinationals and a large presence in Asia, has been tight-lipped about any international tie-ups, but global carriers, particularly from Europe, are said to be aggressively courting NTT to join their own telecom groupings.

At present there are three main global alliances, including Concert, a tie-up between British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp of the United States, and Global One, consisting of Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and America's Sprint Corp.
A third alliance is WorldPartners, a loosely knit organisation assembled by U.S. telecoms giant AT&T.
Some industry officials believe a BT-NTT tie-up may be imminent, as regulatory restrictions on NTT's international services would prompt it to seek a global partner.
But any tie-up would probably be limited, not involving joint ventures or the acquisition of shares, and most likely starting with the leasing of phone lines, they said.
